MODEL CARRIED BY THIS MANIFEST (corrected in R2, unchanged in R3): the Recommendation is an ADVISORY recommendation produced in the Stella analysis/recommendation stage - not a deterministic Score, not a DecisionPolicy result, not a Human Decision, not an approval or certification. The deterministic Score, DecisionPolicy and the Human Decision are each separate. Controls P-8 and N-9 carry that correction, N-15 and M-9 prove the recommendation is not a covert channel into the score, and P-14 / N-14 / M-10 close invariant I2. NAMING DERIVATION: the repo-native convention for a versioned package manifest is <PACKAGE_STEM>_TEST_MANIFEST_v<semver>.json placed beside its authority - measured exemplars are docs/ops/portfolio/PORTFOLIO_COMMERCIAL_V1_TEST_MANIFEST_v1.0.0.json, docs/ops/commercial/COMMERCIAL_ACCOUNT_ENTITLEMENT_TEST_MANIFEST_v1.0.0.json, docs/ops/tenancy/MULTI_ORG_TENANT_SCOPE_TEST_MANIFEST_v1.0.0.json and docs/ops/p1a/P1A_FULL_BOOTSTRAP_TEST_MANIFEST_v1.0.0.json - so the authority stem EVALUATE_V1_AUTHORITY_v1.0.0 yields EVALUATE_V1_TEST_MANIFEST_v1.0.0.json unambiguously. THIS MANIFEST IS A PRE-IMPLEMENTATION COMMITMENT: no node of it exists at AS_OF_HEAD - the repository contains zero Evaluate domain identifiers - so every test_file below is legitimately UNKNOWN. PROTECTED_AUTHORITY DERIVATION: set to the string 'UNKNOWN', not null. The schema documents null as meaning 'no protected surface is touched', which would be false here because protected_surfaces below is deliberately non-empty; the schema's own top-level description requires that unknown or absent required evidence be represented explicitly, naming 'UNKNOWN' as that form so a validator fails closed rather than reading an empty value as satisfied. The three merged precedents that pair null with a non-empty protected_surfaces list are acknowledged and deliberately not followed on that one field; the deviation is recorded as finding F-EV-2 in the companion authority. No grant is allocated by this mission, and no gate reads this field from a manifest file. H2_DECISION_POLICY - BLOCKING and UNKNOWN. DecisionPolicy bands, permitted outcomes and the decider role are defined by zero artifacts at AS_OF_HEAD, and RE_U4 human_decision_matrix[11] records the decider binding itself as TARGET_ONLY. postgres_requirements.rationale: A real PostgreSQL probe is MANDATORY for this batch and both manifest paths are legitimately UNKNOWN because no implementing node exists yet - naming a harness path that does not exist would be a fabricated fact. Static reading of SQL text is NOT proof for any property this batch depends on: row-level security policy combination (PERMISSIVE OR versus RESTRICTIVE AND), NULL-not-TRUE denial, trigger firing order, effective privilege inheritance and constraint behaviour under concurrency are all runtime properties. The probes this batch requires are: cross-organization invisibility of every Evaluate object measured by sentinel IDENTITY rather than by row count, because a count-based assertion cannot distinguish 'denied' from 'no such row'; refusal of an UPDATE against a decided evaluation row, proving the decided-evaluation guard trigger actually fires rather than merely existing; refusal of an UPDATE against a submitted reviewer assessment and against a referenced template version; refusal of a non-project subject at the database boundary, not only in application code; enforcement of separation of duties at the write path; and a privilege census proving no Stella identity holds write privilege on the score, sufficiency, divergence-resolution or decision surfaces - the advisory-recommendation surface being the ONLY Evaluate table a Stella identity may write. HARNESS SHAPE, frozen by the companion authority: a DISPOSABLE cluster only, via the repository's disposable-audit path - NEVER staging, NEVER production, NEVER the canonical local stack. The fixture must be TWO-ORGANIZATION with real rows in the non-scoped organization, because a probe returning zero rows merely for want of data proves nothing.

sentinels.purpose: A uniquely-valued evaluation planted in a second organization. It must never appear in any result set, log line, error payload, export, aggregate or Stella context produced by a request scoped to the first organization. Asserted by IDENTITY rather than by row count, because a count-based assertion cannot distinguish a genuine denial from an empty table.

A second revision of an already-pinned evidence record, carrying a uniquely identifiable value. It must never surface through an evaluation that pinned the earlier version - proving I4 pins a version rather than following a mutable head.

A uniquely-valued string emitted by a stubbed Stella response into every field Stella is permitted to write, including the advisory recommendation. It must never appear in the deterministic score, in any input the scoring engine consumes, in a sufficiency determination, in a divergence resolution, in a DecisionPolicy version or in a decision. Proves Stella non-escalation by identity rather than by inspecting call sites, and specifically proves the advisory recommendation is not a covert channel into the score.

positive_controls.description: IMMUTABLE TEMPLATE VERSIONS: publishing an AssessmentTemplateVersion and referencing it from an evaluation leaves the version's dimensions and criteria byte-identical afterwards, and a subsequent rubric change produces a NEW version while the referencing evaluation continues to resolve the original. Proves I3.

EVIDENCE-VERSION PINNING: an evaluation that pins evidence version V continues to resolve V after a later revision V+1 is created, and the pinned version id is recorded on the evaluation rather than a mutable evidence head. Proves I4. Exercises SENTINEL_UNPINNED_EVIDENCE_REVISION.

DETERMINISTIC SCORE: computing the score twice over the same input set, template version and engine version yields byte-identical output, and the stored score carries an input_set_hash and an engine version that reproduce it. Proves I5. BLOCKED on H1 - the expected string is undefined until N/A arithmetic is ratified.

DECIMAL ARITHMETIC: the engine computes with exact decimal arithmetic across a weighted criteria set chosen so that binary floating point would produce a different last-place digit, and the exact value round-trips through persistence unchanged. Proves the Decimal clause of I5. BLOCKED on H1.
REVIEWER ASSESSMENT LIFECYCLE: a reviewer creates a draft assessment, edits it while draft, and submits it; after submission the assessment is readable and immutable. Proves I6.

DIVERGENCE DETECTION: two reviewers submitting materially different ratings over the same criteria produce a detected divergence, computed over SUBMITTED assessments only - a draft assessment does not contribute. Proves I8 detection.

DIVERGENCE RESOLUTION IS APPEND-ONLY: a human resolves a detected divergence with a recorded rationale; the resolution is appended and both diverging assessments remain readable and unchanged. Proves I8 resolution.

ADVISORY RECOMMENDATION IS PRODUCED IN THE STELLA STAGE: an advisory recommendation is generated in the Stella analysis/recommendation stage, attributed to Stella, stored in its own object distinct from the deterministic score and from any decision, and carrying no governance effect - an evaluation may carry an advisory recommendation with no decision, and its presence neither gates nor unblocks any transition. Proves the positive half of I9. The superseded R1 control asserted the recommendation was produced deterministically from DecisionPolicy over the score, which contradicted the frozen ordering. Shape-BLOCKED on H3.

DECISION AND FINALIZATION: an authorized human records the final decision; the evaluation becomes finalized and its decided state is thereafter immutable. Proves I10 and the RE_U4 exit condition 'Human Decision recorded, immutable'.

CROSS-ORG POSITIVE PATH: an actor scoped to their own organization reads their own evaluations in full. Establishes that the isolation controls N-11 and M-6 are measuring denial rather than a globally broken read path.

STELLA ANALYSIS: Stella produces narrative analysis over an evaluation, stored as advisory content and attributed to Stella rather than to a human actor. Proves the permitted half of the Stella boundary. Shape-BLOCKED on H3.

AUDIT TRACEABILITY: a full evaluation lifecycle emits an audit record for each transition - creation, input submission, evidence pinning, score computation, assessment submission, divergence detection, divergence resolution, advisory recommendation generation, decision and finalization - each carrying actor, organization and timestamp, with Stella actions attributed to Stella. Proves I13.

SEPARATION OF DUTIES POSITIVE PATH: a decider who authored neither an input nor an assessment on the evaluation successfully records the decision. Establishes that N-7 measures a genuine SoD refusal rather than a decision path that is broken for everyone. BLOCKED on H2 for the decider role.

PROJECT SUBJECT ACCEPTED: an evaluation whose subject is a project in the actor's organization is created successfully. Establishes that N-14 measures a genuine subject-kind refusal rather than an evaluation-creation path that is broken for every subject. Proves the positive half of I2.

negative_controls.description: TEMPLATE VERSION MUTATION REFUSED: an attempt to edit the dimensions, criteria or weights of an AssessmentTemplateVersion that any evaluation references is REFUSED. Proves I3 is enforced rather than merely documented.

EVIDENCE HEAD SUBSTITUTION REFUSED: an attempt to repoint an evaluation's evidence reference from a pinned version to a mutable head, or to a different version after finalization, is REFUSED. Proves I4.

MISSING REQUIRED INPUT FAILS CLOSED: scoring an evaluation whose required inputs are incomplete is REFUSED - the engine returns a refusal, not a partial score, not zero, and not a neutral-scored placeholder. Proves I11.
MISSING REQUIRED EVIDENCE FAILS CLOSED: scoring an evaluation whose required evidence is absent or unpinned is REFUSED, with the same no-partial-score guarantee. Proves I11.

REVIEWER-SUPPLIED AGGREGATE REJECTED: an attempt to write a reviewer-supplied aggregate into the score field, or to accept a client-supplied score on any input path, is REFUSED. Proves the INPUT != SCORE edge of I1 and is the specific defect that makes sroi_run_reviews.readiness_score unusable as this batch's substrate.
SUBMITTED ASSESSMENT MUTATION REFUSED: an attempt to edit a reviewer assessment after submission is REFUSED. Proves I6.

SEPARATION OF DUTIES REFUSAL: an actor who authored an input or an assessment on an evaluation attempting to record the final decision on that same evaluation is REFUSED at the write path, and the refusal is itself audit-logged. Proves I7.

UNRESOLVED DIVERGENCE BLOCKS DECISION: recording a decision on an evaluation carrying a material unresolved divergence is REFUSED. Proves the fail-closed clause of I8 and the RE_U4 FAIL_CLOSED_STATE 'unresolved Divergence'.

ADVISORY RECOMMENDATION NEVER BECOMES A DECISION OR A POLICY RESULT: no code path converts an advisory recommendation into a Human Decision without an explicit authorized human act - asserted against elapsed time, against reviewer unanimity and against a maximal confidence value - and no code path accepts an advisory recommendation as a DecisionPolicy result or as a substitute for a DecisionPolicy version. Proves the negative half of I9. Partly BLOCKED on H2.

DECIDED EVALUATION IS IMMUTABLE: an UPDATE against a decided evaluation, its decision row or its score row is REFUSED at the database level by the decided-evaluation guard, not merely by application code. Correction is only available by opening a governed successor referencing the predecessor. Proves I10.

CROSS-ORG READ REFUSED FAIL-CLOSED: a request scoped to organization A for an evaluation belonging to organization B is REFUSED, and the refusal is distinguishable from an empty result. Proves I12. Exercises SENTINEL_FOREIGN_ORG_EVALUATION_CANARY, which must appear in no output of any kind.

STELLA NON-ESCALATION: Stella output is REFUSED as a write to the deterministic score, to a sufficiency determination, to a divergence resolution, to a DecisionPolicy version and to a decision - each asserted separately, including the indirect path where Stella text is written into a field one of those surfaces later reads. Exercises SENTINEL_STELLA_AUTHORED_STRING, which must appear in none of the five. The advisory-recommendation object is the ONLY Evaluate surface a Stella identity may write. Shape-BLOCKED on H3.

EVALUATE VERBS CONFORM TO THE LIVE AUDIT VOCABULARY: every Evaluate audit action value matches the naming pattern that lib/audit/__tests__/logger.test.ts declares as AUDIT_ACTION_VALUE_PATTERN, and none duplicates an existing value. RETARGETED IN R3: the widening this control previously anticipated has LANDED - the pattern is now /^[a-z_]+(\.[a-z_]+)+$/, two or more segments, so the three-segment probe the R2 control relied on is now legitimately ACCEPTED and would no longer prove anything. The axes that still bite, and which this control must assert are still rejected, are a bare unprefixed verb, an uppercase character, an empty middle segment, an empty leading segment and an empty trailing segment. The repository now pins those five forms itself, so this control's remaining job is to bind Evaluate's own verbs to the same named constant rather than to a copied literal - a copied regex would silently diverge the next time the convention moves, which it already has once.

NON-PROJECT SUBJECT REFUSED: creating an evaluation whose subject is anything other than a project - an organization, a portfolio, an SROI run, or another evaluation - is REFUSED at the write path, and the refusal is fail-closed rather than a silent coercion to a default subject. Proves I2. This control commits to a refusal at future implementation time; it does not assert that any subject-kind mechanism exists today, and its test_file is UNKNOWN like every other control here.

ADVISORY RECOMMENDATION NEVER FEEDS THE DETERMINISTIC SCORE: computing the score for an evaluation that carries an advisory recommendation yields a byte-identical result to computing it for the same evaluation with none, and the engine's declared input set does not contain the advisory-recommendation object. Proves that the recommendation channel is not a covert path by which Stella influences the score - the failure mode the superseded R1 model made structurally possible by storing the score and the recommendation in one row. Exercises SENTINEL_STELLA_AUTHORED_STRING. BLOCKED on H1 for the score value itself, but the EQUALITY assertion is testable without H1 because it compares two runs rather than asserting an absolute string.

mutation_controls.description: Deleting the missing-required-input fail-closed branch from the engine MUST make N-3 fail. If N-3 still passes, it is proving the absence of data rather than the presence of a refusal.
Deleting the separation-of-duties check from the decision write path MUST make N-7 fail.
Deleting the unresolved-divergence guard from the decision write path MUST make N-8 fail.

Dropping the decided-evaluation guard trigger MUST make N-10 fail under the real-PostgreSQL probe. A test that still passes without the trigger is proving application-layer behaviour only and would not catch a direct database write.

Replacing the engine's exact decimal arithmetic with IEEE-754 binary floating point MUST make P-3 or P-4 fail. If both still pass, the chosen criteria weights are insufficiently discriminating and the Decimal guarantee is untested.
Removing the organization predicate from an Evaluate read path MUST make N-11 fail and MUST surface SENTINEL_FOREIGN_ORG_EVALUATION_CANARY.
Removing the Stella non-escalation guard MUST make N-12 fail and MUST surface SENTINEL_STELLA_AUTHORED_STRING in at least one of the five prohibited destinations.
Editing a referenced AssessmentTemplateVersion in place MUST make N-1 fail and MUST change what P-1's evaluation resolves - proving immutability is enforced rather than merely conventional.

Wiring the advisory-recommendation object into the scoring engine's input set MUST make N-15 fail. This is the mutation that reproduces the superseded R1 defect at runtime: if N-15 still passes with the recommendation wired in, the equality assertion is comparing two evaluations that both lack a recommendation and is vacuous.

Deleting the subject-kind check from the evaluation-creation write path MUST make N-14 fail. If N-14 still passes, it is proving that the non-project subject could not be constructed by the fixture rather than that it was refused.
